summary: Batch tokenization recount led to missing provisional credit on invoice
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a one-time spike on their provisional invoice for a nightly batch embeddings job. The provisional invoice shows an overage line but the expected provisional credit (hourly buffer / warmup credit) was not applied. The timing coincides with a scheduled tokenizer micro-upgrade that changed token counts for the affected dataset.

Impact:
- Vertex Analytics saw a provisional overage charge of ~USD 1,200 on 2026-03-09 provisional invoice.
- Customer is on Dedicated plan with reserved capacity; unexpected overage caused an autopay failure alert.
- Customer requests explanation and provisional credit reconciliation prior to final invoice.

Environment:
- Customer org: Vertex Analytics (dedicated)
- Region: us-west-2 production
- Job: nightly-batch-embed-v2 (approx 1.2M documents, microbatching)
- Model variants: openlm-embed-3b (quantized variant served during fallback)

Steps to reproduce / Observed sequence:
1) 2026-03-09 01:45 UTC: Tokenizer micro-upgrade (deploy ID: tok-2026-03-09-01) rolled to us-west staging then promoted to prod at 02:10 UTC.
2) 2026-03-09 03:00 UTC: Vertex starts nightly-batch-embed job hitting dedicated endpoints.
3) 2026-03-09 03:05–03:45 UTC: Batch processor reports slightly higher token counts per document (+8% on average) and several files were re-tokenized due to new normalization rules.
4) 2026-03-09 04:00 UTC: Metering postbacks for batch show increased token counts to billing pipeline.
5) 2026-03-09 05:00 UTC: Billing provisional invoice generated without applying the hourly buffer/warmup provisional credit for this job.
6) 2026-03-10: Customer noticed provisional overage and opened support ticket.

Logs / Attachments:
- Attached: sample-postback-entries-2026-03-09.csv (from customer)
steps_to_reproduce: Run nightly-batch-embed-v2 with same input set
Inspect metering postback token counts and compare to pre-upgrade baseline
Check postback windowing and hourly-buffer credit application logs
current_behavior: Batch job token counts increased after tokenizer micro-upgrade and provisional invoice reflected overage without the expected warmup/hourly buffer credit being applied.
expected_behavior: Tokenization changes should update token counts in metering but provisional credits (hourly buffer / warmup) should still be applied to eligible jobs; final invoice should reconcile any provisional overage if mitigation is applied.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Aisha Patel (Support): Opening ticket after customer sent CSV showing token delta. Requested immediate provisional review and whether a temporary credit can be issued.
2026-03-10 10:05 - Diego Morales (Billing Eng): Acknowledged — asked for postback IDs, sample payloads, and the customer's scheduled job ID. Assigned to meter-ingest on-call.

2026-03-10 11:20 - Customer (Vertex Analytics - Sara Kim): Provided sample-postback-entries-2026-03-09.csv and clarified that they expect warmup credits for the first 2 hours of the job per their dedicated contract.

2026-03-10 13:40 - Diego Morales (Billing Eng): Found discrepancy: meter-service emitted higher token counts and a small subset of postbacks were reissued (duplicate postback pattern) during re-tokenization window. Asking SRE to check for duplicate suppression failure.

2026-03-10 16:00 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Confirmed duplicate postbacks (3xx/5xx retry loop) observed for postback shard 17 between 03:07–03:20 UTC; de-dupe worker lagged behind due to GC event. Filing INT-391 for de-dupe worker fix.

2026-03-11 08:30 - Diego Morales (Billing Eng): Calculated approximate over-count attributable to duplicates (~6% of reported tokens) and additional ~2% due to tokenization rule changes. Requested billing to hold final invoice while we reconcile provisional credits.
2026-03-11 12:10 - Support (Aisha): Notified customer we are investigating and asked patience; promised provisional hold decision within SLA window.
2026-03-12 09:00 - Finance (Maya Singh): Approved provisional hold for final invoice pending reconciliation; requested documented delta and proposed credit amount before release.
2026-03-12 11:30 - Diego Morales: Posted reconciliation summary and proposed credits to ticket thread (see investigation_notes).
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: Tokenizer upgrade increased token counts which caused legitimate higher usage — requires customer-facing explanation.
Secondary hypothesis: Duplicate postbacks during re-tokenization window caused inflated metering leading to overcharge; de-dupe lag observed in logs and linked to GC pause on de-dupe-worker-17.

Metering analysis: Aggregated postbacks for job nightly-batch-embed-v2 between 03:00–04:00 UTC; total tokens reported: 13,480,912. Pre-upgrade baseline average for same job historically: 12,400,000 (+8.7%).
  - Duplicates identified: ~748,000 tokens (approx 5.5% of reported), confirmed by identical postback fingerprints re-ingested with new token counts after re-tokenize pass.
  - Tokenizer delta: ~332,000 tokens (approx 2.5%) attributable to changed normalization (emoji decomposition + new punctuation rules).

Billing pipeline: Hourly buffer/warmup credit calculation triggers during ingestion window; check shows credit was not attached because the postback aggregator marked the job as 'non-eligible' for buffer due to a transient job-tag metadata mismatch introduced by the batch-processor update at 02:58 UTC.

Root causes (combined): 1) Duplicate postbacks during re-tokenization due to de-dupe-worker GC pause; 2) Batch-processor metadata tag rename (tag: warmup_elig -> warmup_eligible) resulted in missing eligibility flag for credit application; 3) Tokenizer change contributed small natural token increase but not the majority of overage.
resolution_notes:
Mitigation steps taken (2026-03-12):
1) Billing placed provisional hold on final invoice for Vertex Analytics pending reconciliation (Finance approval).
2) Issued a provisional credit of USD 720 to offset the duplicate-postback portion while full reconciliation completes.
3) Hotfix deployed to de-dupe worker to prevent GC-induced re-ingestion (INT-391 linked).
4) Batch-processor tag mapping rollback applied to restore warmup eligibility for reprocessed postbacks; re-run of aggregator scheduled for 2026-03-12 22:00 UTC.

Planned follow-ups:
- Re-run postback aggregation for the 2026-03-09 window and recompute final token totals (Owner: Diego Morales) by 2026-03-13.
- Generate formal reconciliation statement and proposed final credit (Owner: Finance - Maya Singh) by 2026-03-13.
- Add monitoring alert for de-dupe-worker GC pauses and tag-mapping drift (Owner: SRE).
- Communicate outcome to customer with breakdown and final invoice adjustment or waiver as appropriate.

Customer communication:
- 2026-03-12 15:00 Support informed customer of provisional credit and hold; they acknowledged and requested final reconciliation.
outcome_expected: Final invoice will be adjusted to remove duplicate-induced tokens and reapply eligible warmup/hourly buffer credits; customer to receive full reconciliation report and either invoice adjustment or waiver depending on final delta.
